catalog_quote: I carried out preliminary fieldwork in Tilé Nougar in 2014 (one day), 2017 (one week), and 2020 (one week). The preliminary data shows that: Kulaale vowels have an advanced tongue root (ATR) contrast and harmony; the tone system is characterized by two contrastive heights, with frequent use of polar tone and complex non-concatenative tonal morphology; verbs have complex morphology with three moods (indicative, subjunctive, infinitive), and a derived instrumental form (‘do X with’), in all three moods; a focus suffix is used on all verbal forms (simple and associative forms, all moods) when an element in the utterance is focused. new_statements.rule_in_words: Fania/Kulaale is a tone language with two contrastive pitch heights (H/L), polar tone and grammatical (non-concatenative) tonal morphology. No source examined says anything about word stress or accent placement — neither a rule, nor that stress is non-contrastive, nor that it is absent. The only modern first-hand description is a 2020 language snapshot based on about two weeks of fieldwork; the reference grammar from the 2020-2025 NSF project has not appeared.
new_statements.exceptions: None; no stress rule is given.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statement is about the lexical/grammatical tone system (word level); Boyeldieu et al. 2018 (Table 3, p.5-6) add second-hand that Kulaale/Fanya contrasts mood/aspect on the verb by tone change. Nothing about phrase-level prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: Lionnet's 'Kulaale' [kʊ̀láálɛ́] (speakers Kulaawe/Eywe) is the same language as Glottolog fani1244 'Fania' [fni]; his data come from the single village of Tilé Nougar (blacksmith community). Boyeldieu et al. 2018 reserve 'Kulaale' for Lionnet's data and 'Fanya' for older sources (Joly 1935; Faris & Meundeung 1993c from Rim and Sissi; Khalil Alio's list) and note variation among Fanya varieties (h- ~ f-). Do not confuse with Kulaal = Gula Iro (gula1265 [glj]), a different Bua language whose stress/tone statement (Pairault 1969) is already recorded under gula1265.

sources.locator: §2 'Current research', p. 131 (and §1 p. 130 on prior documentation)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. §2 'Current research' (p.131) reports from 2014/2017/2020 fieldwork in Tilé Nougar that vowels have ATR harmony and 'the tone system is characterized by two contrastive heights, with frequent use of polar tone and complex non-concatenative tonal morphology'. p.130: the language is 'virtually undocumented'; the only prior data are four short wordlists (Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1906, Joly 1935, Faris & Meundeung 1993, Khalil Alio 2005), 'tone is not transcribed' in all but the last.

Table 3 (p.5) marks 'verb tone contrast' as + for Fanya and p.6 says 'The only Inland language that seems to share this feature [mood/aspect contrast by tone changes on the verb] is Kulaale/Fanya'; §4.4 Tones (p.12) and §5.5 (p.24) give tone data only for Ba, Lua, Tun, Bolgo and Kulaal, none for Fanya. pp.2-4 list the Fanya sources: Joly 1935, Faris & Meundeung 1993c (Rim, Sissi), unpublished wordlist by Alio Khalil, Lionnet field notes (Kulaale).
